message.content:
`docker start` is used to start **containers**, not the Docker daemon itself. If you want to bring up the Docker service (the Docker Engine) on Windows, you have a couple of options: | What you want to do | How to do it | |---------------------|--------------| | **Start the Docker Desktop GUI** | `Start-Process -FilePath "C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"` (PowerShell) | | **Start the Docker Engine service** | `net start com.docker.service` (Command Prompt)
or `Start-Service Docker` (PowerShell) | | **Start a specific container** | `docker start ` | ### Quick Commands ```powershell # 1️⃣ Start Docker Desktop (GUI) Start-Process -FilePath "C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe" # 2️⃣ Start the Docker Engine service (no GUI) Start-Service Docker # PowerShell # or net start com.docker.service # Command Prompt # 3️⃣ Start a container (replace with your container name or ID) docker start ``` > **Tip:** If you’re using Docker Desktop, simply launching the Docker Desktop executable will automatically start the Docker Engine in the background. > If you’re using Docker Machine or a Linux VM on Windows, you’d use `docker-machine start ` instead. Let me know which scenario fits your setup, or if you need help with a specific container name!
